function.mechanism: Hydrolyzes sucrose into glucose and fructose (invert sugar).
common_food_categories: general food manufacturing enzyme uses under cGMP

adi.basis: No numerical ADI was set in the latest EFSA invertase food-enzyme opinion (2024); conclusion was no safety concern under intended use.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA FEZ (2024, e9128) concluded beta-fructofuranosidase from Saccharomyces cerevisiae does not give rise to safety concerns under intended conditions of use.

fda.cfr_citation: 21 CFR 184.1(b) (cGMP framework for affirmed GRAS direct food ingredients); 21 CFR 170.3(o) (technical effects). No invertase-specific named section was found in current eCFR Title 21 XML.

adi.basis: WHO/JECFA database lists ADI as 'NOT SPECIFIED' for invertase from Saccharomyces cerevisiae (ID 1726).

concerns.summary: EFSA evaluations note that dietary allergic reactions cannot be excluded; one dossier found sequence homology with a tomato allergen, but overall likelihood was described as low.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2024 invertase opinion concluded no safety concern under intended conditions of use.
Recent EFSA 2025/2026 beta-fructofuranosidase evaluations reported no genotoxicity concern and high NOAEL values in 90-day studies where required.
JECFA assigned ADI 'not specified' with GMP-limited use.

populations: tomato-allergic individuals (potential low-likelihood sensitivity flagged in one EFSA dossier)
adi_exceedance.notes: No numeric ADI was established by EFSA/JECFA for invertase, so standard ADI exceedance analysis is not directly applicable.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory evaluations are consistently favorable (EFSA no-safety-concern conclusions; JECFA ADI not specified with GMP controls; FDA GRAS notice with no-questions outcome). No IARC carcinogenic classification was identified. Main residual uncertainty is low-probability allergenicity in sensitive individuals.
key_factors: EFSA 2024 conclusion of no safety concern under intended use
JECFA ADI not specified (2001) with GMP limitation
FDA GRAS notice GRN 88 closed with 'FDA has no questions'
No IARC listing/classification found for invertase
